one_liner: Clang-plugin source-transformation AD for C++ generating derivative source code; no published timing against other AD tools.
what_it_does: Clad is a Clang compiler plugin that reads a C++ function's AST and emits new C++ functions computing its derivative: clad::differentiate (forward mode), clad::gradient (reverse mode), clad::hessian, clad::jacobian (vectorized forward mode) and clad::estimate_error (floating-point error estimation). You mark functions in ordinary source, compile with -fplugin=clad.so, and call the returned functor's execute() with caller-allocated, zeroed derivative storage; the generated code can be dumped or written to a file. Unlike operator-overloading tools it needs no active type, but every function it reaches must have a visible body or a user-supplied custom derivative.
how_it_is_fast: Source transformation: the derivative is plain C++ that the compiler optimizes together with the primal, so there is no operator-overloading or tape-interpretation overhead at run time. In reverse mode a to-be-recorded (TBR) analysis decides which overwritten values must be pushed on a clad::tape, so statements like y = y + x*i store nothing, and activity analysis skips inactive variables. Release 2.5 recomputes counted-loop trip counts in the reverse sweep and accumulates broadcast-read adjoints in registers; 2.3 added a tape that can offload to disk.
when_to_use: Gradients of self-contained numeric C++ kernels (likelihoods, cost functions, physics formulas) with many inputs and one output, where you control the source and compile with upstream Clang 14-23
When you want to read, debug or ship the derivative as source code (dump(), -fgenerate-source-file) instead of a runtime tape

ROOT/RooFit users: Clad is the AD engine behind RooFit's code-generation path; the ACAT 2022 paper and ROOT blog report a 5.5x faster minimization for about 1,000 parameters versus numerical gradients (search-result snippets, pages blocked here)
Interactive work in Jupyter through xeus-cpp/clang-repl (conda-forge packages)
Floating-point error estimation of a function, which operator-overloading AD libraries do not offer
when_not_to_use: If you need evidence that it beats another AD tool: the repo ships Google Benchmark sources (Enzyme, Tapenade memory, vector mode, Hessians, GPT-2) but publishes no results
Code that calls functions defined in other translation units or binary-only libraries, uses virtual methods (unsupported per issue 2176), exceptions, goto or reference data members
GCC, MSVC or Apple Clang builds: the plugin only loads into the exact upstream Clang it was built against
OpenMP-parallel reverse sweeps: open issue 2114 reports a race that gives a different wrong gradient on each multithreaded run
Teams that cannot absorb an evolving tool: 144 open issues, several of them wrong-derivative reports opened in September 2026

integration.dependencies: LLVM/Clang 14.0.x-23.2.x development libraries (plugin clad.so plus the clad/Differentiator headers); optional Enzyme backend built via -DCLAD_ENABLE_ENZYME_BACKEND; conda-forge package available
integration.min_toolchain: Upstream Clang 14 to 23 (same version Clad was built against); README says Clad needs C++14 features and its examples compile with -std=c++17
integration.platforms: Linux and macOS with upstream LLVM (Apple Clang disables plugins); Windows via WSL2 per README; CUDA device code partly supported (issue 2172)
integration.thread_safety: not documented; generated derivatives are ordinary functions whose tapes are local variables, but OpenMP-parallel reverse mode has open race and crash issues (2114, 1852)

gotchas: If Clad cannot differentiate a function it silently falls back to numerical (finite-difference) differentiation; compile with -DCLAD_NO_NUM_DIFF to make that an error
Integer and char variables are differentiated like reals and lossy casts are not warned about, which the README says can give incorrect derivatives
Open wrong-derivative bugs without diagnostics: reference data members double the gradient (issue 2082), forward mode drops output-parameter tangents (2075), reverse mode drops pointer casts (2099)
The caller must allocate and zero gradient and Hessian storage; stale values are accumulated into
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Clad over CoDiPack, XAD or Adept 2 when your code is self-contained C++ compiled with upstream Clang and you want compiler-optimized derivative source without an active type; pick the operator-overloading tools for code spread across libraries, virtual dispatch or GCC/MSVC builds. Pick Enzyme instead when you need multi-language or LLVM-IR-level AD with published speedups (Enzyme reports 4.5x over AD on unoptimized IR); Clad's own Enzyme backend exists mainly for cross-validation.
verified_claims_summary: Nothing measured: the repo's benchmark/ directory contains Google Benchmark comparisons of Clad against its own Enzyme backend, Tapenade (memory), vector forward mode, Hessians and a GPT-2 training run (built -O3 -ffast-math), but no committed results, hardware or compiler versions. The only numbers seen are snippet-level reports of RooFit gradients (5.5x faster minimization at about 1,000 parameters) versus finite differences, which is not another AD tool.
status_note: Very active (release 2.5 on 28 September 2026, last commit 2026-09-30, 2,128 commits) and LGPL-3.0, but correctness bugs are still being filed at a steady rate, so validate derivatives against finite differences before relying on them.
sources_read: WebSearch: RooFit Clad automatic differentiation speedup (snippets of arxiv.org/pdf/2304.02650 and root.cern/blog/roofit-ad; pages not opened)
